title: SAMPLE ENCYCLOTRON AUDIT Why a 20-year-old iconic software company is invisible in AI search — and what it means for you
creator: Rex Fraction
description:
This demonstration applies a shortened Encyclotron battery to Basecamp/37signals. Across fifteen queries and five diagnostic levels, it reports an overall R1 commoditization regime, beige score of 0.71, absence from a selected category query, unfavorable customer-decision framing, intact attribution for Shape Up, strong founder recognition, low unsupported invention, high loss of company philosophy, and fragmentation among product, method, and founder.

The report’s core diagnosis is that Basecamp’s meaning survives where it does not monetize and disappears where purchasing decisions are made. It proposes entity stitching, decision-layer recoding, structured-data deployment, and citation architecture as responses. Because the audit is a promotional demonstration rather than a deposited dataset with complete verbatim outputs in this body, its scores, traffic estimates, revenue model, and causal claims should be represented as author-reported findings. Its archive function is to show how the abstract metrics would appear in a client-facing audit.
reading: Search → Direction → Threshold → Play → Foundation → Proof
wiki_article:
**Sample Encyclotron Audit** is a demonstration report by Rex Fraction applying the Retrieval Architecture diagnostic framework to Basecamp, the project-management product associated with 37signals.

The report runs fifteen queries across entity recognition, competitive position, intellectual property, customer decision, and founder identity. It reports a beige threshold of 0.71, absence from one selected “best software” overview, negative decision-layer framing, accurate attribution of the Shape Up methodology, a strong DHH founder entity, and weak connection among those three surfaces. The audit classifies the overall representation as R1 commoditization with localized R2 capital erasure.

Its main interpretive claim is that the retrieval layer preserves Basecamp’s features and separately preserves its intellectual and founder assets but removes the company’s philosophy from high-value commercial questions. The proposed remedy is to reconnect product, method, and founder through structured entity and citation architecture. The report is both a worked example and a service demonstration. Its measurements and revenue estimates are those of the author’s audit and require independent reproduction before being treated as general facts.
